meaning: Batch Read in word units, D100, 3 points. The worked 3E binary request.
section: 4.2 p.23 layout; JY997D56001-K p.19 prints the same 11-byte prefix
note: L = 000CH = 12 = monitoring timer (2) + command (2) + subcommand (2) + 6 bytes of request data. Total frame 21 bytes = 9 + L.

meaning: Normal completion, three words 1995H 1202H 1130H.
note: L counts from the end code: 2 + 6 = 8.

meaning: The 11-byte minimum normal response: end code only, no response data.
note: A parser that expects data after the end code breaks here. The FX5U returns exactly this frame for 1401 and for 1402 (measured, 2026-09-06).

meaning: Abnormal completion C051H: too many bit points for a batch read.
note: The manual prints the first 16 bytes as hex and labels the remaining command and subcommand echo in its field table rather than printing them; L = 000BH = 2 + 5 + 4 accounts for all 20. The bench captured 16 complete frames of exactly this shape, all 20 bytes with L = 000BH.

meaning: The same Batch Read in ASCII coding: 42 characters, L = 0018H = 24.
note: The SAME request is 000CH = 12 in binary and 0018H = 24 in ASCII. L counts wire units, never binary-equivalent bytes. The device number is '000100' -- D's radix is decimal -- not the hexadecimal of 100.

meaning: The same normal completion in ASCII: 34 characters, L = 0010H = 16.
note: 16 = 4 for the end code + 12 for three 4-character words.

meaning: Abnormal completion in ASCII: 40 characters, L = 0016H = 22.
note: The manual prints the first 32 character codes verbatim (44 30 30 30 ...), which is what makes this row authoritative, and labels the trailing '0401' '0000' command echo in its field table. 22 = 4 + 10 + 8.

meaning: The same request as a 4E frame, serial 0001H. Total 25 bytes = 13 + L.
note: L is computed identically to 3E: the subheader is not counted. Nothing but the subheader moves.

meaning: The same 4E request in ASCII: 50 characters = 26 + 24.
note: Serial 1234H is '1234' in ASCII and 34 12 in binary: most significant first there, least significant first here (p.18 'Point' box). The two codings are not byte transformations of one another.

meaning: Batch Read, D350, 2 word points. 015EH = 350, code A8H = D.

meaning: Read Random: 4 word points (D0, TN0, M100, X20) then 3 double-word points (D1500, Y160, M1111). The manual's own worked example.
note: The payload is opaque to the frame layer, which is the point of this row: L, the prefix and the point-count bytes are checked without any address parsing. meaning: Read Random reply: four word results then three double-word results, all word results first, in the requested order.

meaning: Batch Read D0-D9, the live control block. p1_sanity.log.
note: Monitoring timer 0010H. JY997D56001-K p.27 says to specify 0000H for the CPU module, but 0000H, 0010H, 0028H and 00F0H were all answered normally in ~7 ms: the field is inert on this port, not refused.

meaning: D0-D9: setpoint 60.0000, process value 58.0090, output 23.8921, error 1.9910, scan counter. Every f32 low word first.
Read Random, 3 word points, 0 double-word points. p1_sanity.log.
The same three addresses as double-word access points: one IEEE-754 f32 each, three floats in one 7 ms round trip.
note: Byte for byte the word-access request with the two point-count bytes swapped, which is why the point counts are validated client-side.

meaning: 60.0000, 23.8921 and the scan counter, low word first, in one snapshot.
Write Random: D100=1111H, D101=2222H, D102=3333H and D104/D105 = the f32 1234.5 as one double-word point (00 50 9A 44).
note: Read back as D104 = 5000H, D105 = 449AH: low word first, one of the four independent proofs of the word order.

meaning: Write Random answered with the 11-byte minimum frame: no response data.
Self Test with loopback data 'ABCD': the zero-side-effect health probe the connect handshake uses. 7.34 ms at p50 over 300 samples.
note: The payload is a 2-byte length then the data. 41 42 43 44 are the exact bytes proven on the bench and are the default of Plc.self_test().

meaning: Read Type Name: 'FX5U-32MT/DS    ' (16 characters, space padded, ASCII even in binary coding) then model code 4A49H little-endian.
note: This is the frame the connect handshake matches against profile.model_codes. 49 4A reads as 0x4A49.

meaning: D7999, one point: the last legal D on this CPU. D8000 returns C056H.
D8000, one point: the first D beyond this CPU's range. D7999 with TWO points returns the same code -- the span is what matters, not the start.
ZERO word points from D0. A point-count error, not an address error -- correcting our doc-derived map, which predicted an address error. 961 points returns the same C052H.

Device code 00H. C05CH, NOT the C05BH our doc-derived map predicted. Code FFH, V0, ZR0 and DX0 all return C05CH too: on this CPU 'a device family this CPU does not have' and 'a garbage device code byte' are one code.
193 word access points in one Read Random. 192 is the measured ceiling on the built-in port: word points + double-word points <= 192.
Monitor Register is not supported on iQ-F: the command itself is rejected. 0802 Execute Monitor returns C059H as well, not C05DH, so there is no way to mistake it for 'you forgot to register'.
Execute Monitor, same refusal. Capability-gated pre-transport in aslmp.
The shortest legal request: L = 0006H, monitoring timer, command and subcommand, no request data.
An unknown command is echoed verbatim in the error frame.
A request that declared L = 000AH for a 12-byte body. C061H, NOT the C057H our doc-derived map predicted, and the connection recovered.
note: The same request with L OVERSTATED by 2 produced NO RESPONSE AT ALL: the CPU blocks waiting for bytes that never come. That asymmetry is why L is computed in exactly one expression and guarded three ways.

meaning: A request that declared L = 0000H. The error frame echoes command 0000H subcommand 0000H, because the CPU read the command out of the two bytes a correctly framed request uses for the monitoring timer.
A 4E frame sent to a connection entry configured for 3E. Serial 1234H, little-endian on the wire as 34 12.
note: JY997D56001-K section 2.1 and JY997D56201-B p.25 both say the FX5 built-in port speaks 3E only. It answered this normally. One unit, one firmware: aslmp permits 4E on iQ-F and does not default to it.

meaning: The 4E reply: subheader D400H, serial echoed correctly, D0/D1 = 60.0.
The A-3 probe: AA 55 deliberately placed in the two subheader units after the serial, to find out whether SH(NA)-080008-AB's '(Free)' label is right.
not_buildable_because: aslmp always transmits 0000H there, following SH(NA)-080956ENG-M p.18's '(Fixed value)' and the measurement below. The library cannot emit this frame, so only the parse direction is asserted for this row -- the exclusion is data rather than a silently missing assertion.

meaning: The answer to A-3: the serial was echoed, the AA 55 tail came back 00 00. Not echoed, not rejected. SH(NA)-080956ENG-M's '(Fixed value)' is right and SH(NA)-080008-AB's '(Free)' is wrong: those two units are not 16 free bits of correlation and aslmp builds nothing on them.
